title: kith-tslocal: Status client over Unix socket
description:
Implement async status() -> Result<StatusResponse, AuthError> over Unix socket.

What: HTTP GET /localapi/v0/status to tailscaled Unix socket. Called once at startup.

Algorithm (same socket pattern as whois):
1. Implement status(&self) -> Result<StatusResponse, AuthError> on LocalApiClient:
   a. Connect: tokio::net::UnixStream::connect(&self.socket_path).await map_err -> WhoIsFailed
   b. Wrap + handshake (same as whois)
   c. Build request: GET /localapi/v0/status with Host: local header
   d. Send, check status, collect body (same pattern as whois)
   e. Size check: 10MB limit (status includes all peers, larger than whois)
   f. Parse JSON: serde_json::from_slice -> StatusResponse
   g. Validate: if result.tailscale_ips.is_empty() -> WhoIsFailed('no tailnet IPs - is tailscale running?')
   h. Return Ok(result)
2. Caller (kithd startup) should treat error as fatal: log and exit

Defensive rules:
- Size limit 10MB (status can be large with many peers)
- Validate tailscale_ips non-empty (kithd cannot bind without them)
- All errors -> AuthError::WhoIsFailed(String)
- Do not cache result in kith-tslocal; caching is caller's responsibility
- Backend state 'Running' is expected; caller may check backend_state field
